Substance verified TRUE via gate_admission.py:187-194 (required-on-root + mounted-on-volume predicate)
findings.finding: The marker-design premise is anchored to the wrong source lines: the plan cites 'user_data.sh:123-130' for the placement of .gate-scratch-required (ROOT) and .gate-scratch-mounted (VOLUME), but lines 123-130 are the resolve_ebs_device readlink/by-id fallback block. findings.checklist_item: Add an explicit step (and an AC assertion) to recreate/restart the review-bot container after the host mount so the new mount propagates into its /var/lib/rebar bind namespace, and verify the mount is visible FROM INSIDE the container (e.g. `docker compose exec review-bot mountpoint -q /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` and proof-marker visibility), not only from the host.
evidence: docker-compose.yml:305 `- /var/lib/rebar:/var/lib/rebar` — a plain bind of the mount's PARENT with no propagation suffix (default rprivate)
docker-compose.yml:293-299 states the bind is at the PARENT deliberately so the marker guard works — but this same design means a post-start host mount is not seen inside the container
Plan step 1 only says 'Confirm no gate/review is in flight'; no step stops or recreates the review-bot container

AC3 proves gate_scratch_mounted from CloudWatch/observability.sh, which runs on the HOST (observability.sh:211) and will read 1 regardless of what the container sees — so it does not detect the propagation gap
findings.finding: The remediation sequence mounts the volume on the host but never recreates/restarts the review-bot container, which binds /var/lib/rebar at Docker's default rprivate propagation; a host mount created while the container runs will not propagate into the container, so the in-container gate_admission consumer keeps seeing proof-absent (or writes to the shadowed pre-mount directory) and the goal of moving gate scratch off root for the running consumer is not actually achieved.
findings.location: Remediation section steps 1-7 and AC3; infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:305
scenarios: Operator runs the sequence with the review-bot container up; host lsblk/mountpoint pass and gate_scratch_mounted flips to 1, but the container's gate_admission still refuses because the proof marker is invisible in its namespace, or the bot silently keeps writing to root under the shadow mount
findings.suggested_fix: After step 5, add: `docker compose -f infra/compose/docker-compose.yml up -d --force-recreate review-bot` (or stop it before mounting and start it after), then assert the mount and .gate-scratch-mounted marker are visible inside the container; alternatively change the compose bind to a shared/rslave propagation and document that as the mechanism that lets a post-boot host mount reach the container.

findings.checklist_item: Choose one AC5 mechanism (post-boot auto-mount vs. apply-time signal) and, for the chosen one, state how it deploys and how it is cheaply reverted if it misbehaves.
evidence: AC5 offers two distinct designs joined by 'or' — an automatic post-boot mounter (a persistent behavior change on every boot) vs. an apply-time assertion (a terraform check).
The two options have materially different rollout/rollback surfaces (a boot-time auto-mount runs on all future boots and needs its own revert path; an apply-time check gates terraform runs).
findings.finding: AC5 leaves the delivery-gap fix as two mutually-exclusive alternatives ('mounted by something that runs post-boot, OR its absence is made a loud, actionable signal at apply time') without choosing one, so the code deliverable's shape — and therefore how it rolls out and how it is reverted — is unspecified. This under-specifies both the mechanism and its rollback path for the code portion.

findings.checklist_item: [ ] In AC5, enumerate and briefly weigh the established mechanisms for the post-boot provisioning gap (e.g. SSM State Manager/RunCommand association, cloud-init per-boot script, Terraform remote-exec/null_resource trigger for the 'mount post-boot' route; Terraform precondition or the existing gate_scratch_mounted drift alarm for the 'loud apply-time signal' route) and state which is chosen and why, rather than leaving the mechanism unspecified.
evidence: Plan text: 'either mounted by something that runs post-boot, or its absence is made a loud, actionable signal at apply time' — names two design directions but zero candidate mechanisms.
Plan's own root cause ('user_data.sh runs under cloud-init on FIRST BOOT ONLY') is the textbook description of a well-documented failure category.

Retrieved prior art (StackOverflow 'How to mount a ebs_block_device using Terraform', HashiCorp 'Detect infrastructure drift and enforce policies', Terraform aws_volume_attachment registry docs, AWS re:Post 'allow user data to run after first boot') confirms established remediations exist: remote-exec/null_resource provisioners, SSM State Manager/RunCommand post-boot associations, cloud-init per-boot scripts, and Terraform preconditions/drift-detection for the apply-time-signal route.

ABSENCE: the plan cites no ADR, no existing repo mechanism, and no external approach for the generic fix, despite the repo already carrying SSM (infra/terraform/ssm.tf) and drift-observability tooling that are candidate prior art.
findings.finding: AC5 mandates closing the post-boot delivery gap ('a volume added by terraform apply after first boot is either mounted by something that runs post-boot, or its absence is made a loud, actionable signal at apply time') but considers no established mechanism for either direction, so the implementer is left to reinvent a solution to a well-known problem.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — final AC5 bullet ('The DELIVERY GAP is closed, not just this instance')
scenarios: An implementer picks an ad-hoc post-boot mount hack (e.g. a bespoke cron/systemd unit) when SSM State Manager or a Terraform precondition would be the idiomatic, already-in-repo choice.
The 'loud signal at apply time' option is chosen but reinvents drift detection that Terraform preconditions / the existing gate_scratch_mounted alarm already provide.
